assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall state as a topological phase protected by time-reversal symmetry, and its observation, opened the field of topological band theory and has had very wide influence on condensed matter, photonics and materials science. The core idea is a clean, general mechanism (a Z2 invariant and protected edge states) that I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory (graphene QSH proposal and the Z2 classification). Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not in the credited list. The 3D topological insulator strand and Hasan's ARPES work are a separable part that may complicate a three-person split; I choose the theory-plus-first-experiment trio.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation across materials, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue, though the neighbouring 2016 prize on topological phase transitions makes the novelty case a little more delicate.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) lies outside the supplied names.
Whether the prize should cover 2D QSH only or also 3D topological insulators is unresolved.
Experimental priority between QSH in HgTe and 3D materials is partly entangled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: KPZ universality is a prime example of a simple stochastic growth equation whose scaling exponents and fluctuation statistics (Tracy-Widom/Baik-Rains) are universal across a huge range of systems. Takeuchi's liquid-crystal experiments gave the first precise confirmation of the exact distributions. It links non-equilibrium statistical physics, random-matrix theory and integrable probability, which makes it very attractive from my perspective.
assessment.attribution: The KPZ equation was introduced by Kardar, Parisi and Zhang, and Parisi is not among the credited names; this is a real fairness problem for the theoretical founders. Takeuchi and Sano gave the decisive experimental confirmation. Exact solutions came from mathematicians (Johansson, Prahofer-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel, Sasamoto-Spohn), who are also not credited.
assessment.maturity: The theory dates from 1986 and the experimental confirmation from 2010-2011, and the exact solutions are mature. Interpretation is stable, though experimental realisations of the full universality class remain few. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Omission of Parisi from the credited names makes a clean attribution hard.
Role of the mathematical exact-solution work in the prize citation is unresolved.
Technological or broad experimental impact is smaller than for other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method, survey propagation and the statistical-physics treatment of random constraint satisfaction and inference give a rigorous and general account of phase transitions in computational problems. They connect spin glasses to computer science, coding and machine learning, and fit my interest in statistical mechanics of learning.
assessment.attribution: Mézard and Zecchina made the decisive contributions to the cavity method for finite-connectivity problems, the random k-SAT analysis and survey propagation. Montanari's contributions are more on message-passing, coding and inference, so a two-person configuration is defensible. The foundation of the replica and cavity ideas lies with Parisi (2021 prize), which affects how much remains for a new prize.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established with rigorous mathematical confirmation (e.g. Talagrand, Ding-Sly-Sun) and widespread use. Overlap with the 2021 and 2024 prizes could make recognition seem partly already given.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2021 spin-glass prize and the 2024 neural-network prize.
Experimental and physical-system impact is less direct than for other candidates.
Division of credit with Montanari and other contributors such as Mulet, Pagnani, Weigt.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping, brought fractional uncertainties to the 10^-18 level and enables tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. The idea is clean and the impact on precision measurement is major.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and Ye's group carried out the most precise realisations; the two-person configuration is natural. Hall and Haensch's combs were already recognised in 2005 and Wineland's ion clocks in 2012, so this recognises a complementary step.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories with stable interpretation. Redefinition of the SI second is still pending, so there is a case for waiting, but the physics is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes on combs and ion clocks.
Whether the Nobel committee sees this as an incremental step beyond 2012.
Role of other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Schmidt) is outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry's geometric phase are foundational, universal concepts that underlie much of modern physics, from topological matter to molecular dynamics. They are the kind of paper that 'already contained almost everything'. The significance is lasting and clearly understood.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) gave the effect, with Bohm deceased and Ehrenberg-Siday earlier; Berry (1984) gave the geometric phase, with Pancharatnam's earlier work. The two-person configuration omits Bohm and so is only partly fair to the Aharonov-Bohm strand. The two discoveries are also separate and could need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for decades (Chambers, Tonomura, optical and NMR tests of Berry phase). Recognition is very late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Bohm, Pancharatnam and Ehrenberg-Siday priority claims complicate attribution.
The compound candidate joins two discoveries of different date and character.
Nobel history shows hesitation toward foundational-concept prizes without direct application.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire engineering, a rich and rapidly growing field with a simple geometric mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key continuum-model prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group gave the decisive 2018 experiments. The trio is clean, though Cao and others, and earlier work by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, are relevant to credit.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is about eight years old. Many replications exist, but the mechanism of superconductivity and the correlated phases is still debated, so the field may be premature.
uncertainties: Unresolved origin of superconductivity.
Credit for earlier theory (Lopes dos Santos et al.) and for the lead experimenter Yuan Cao.
Timeliness relative to field maturity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming phase diagram gives a unifying picture of how disordered packings of grains, foams and emulsions become rigid, with critical scaling and universal features. It is a simple, general mechanism close to my own interests in soft matter and disordered systems.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram (1998) and the two-person configuration is natural; O'Hern, Silbert, Langer and Wyart contributed to the quantitative picture and the point-J critical behaviour.
assessment.maturity: The mean-field picture and its connections to glass physics are still evolving, and the experimental confirmation is less crisp than for other candidates. Possibly early for a prize.
uncertainties: Contested connection to the glass transition and amorphous solids.
Credit for the point-J scaling work by O'Hern, Silbert and Wyart.
Limited broad impact outside soft matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The three-step recollision picture of strong-field ionisation and the quantum theory of high harmonic generation form the conceptual foundation of attosecond science. It is a simple and general mechanism that was then developed rigorously.
assessment.attribution: Corkum gave the semiclassical recollision model (1993) and Lewenstein with co-workers the quantum theory; Kulander and Schafer's work is closely related. The 2023 prize to Agostini, Krausz and L'Huillier recognised the experimental pulses and left the recollision picture partly uncredited.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed over three decades, with a stable interpretation. Recognition would be timely, although the 2023 prize partly overlaps.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 attosecond prize.
Credit for Kulander and Schafer is outside the supplied names.
Whether the committee views this as separate from the 2023 recognition.
